statement: The trial command of gap gate-slow:test/multiply.test.mjs ran twice in the tree on linux with v24.9.0 and took 10590 ms and 10477 ms of wall time (9 of 9 tests passing and 9 of 9 tests passing), against a bar of 15000 ms where the ledger measured 28924 ms, so barMet is true. The control, the same command on test/multiply.test.mjs and daemon/multiply.mjs as committed at 596b011, took 34382 ms and 33967 ms (9 of 9 passing and 9 of 9 passing). Run-to-run noise was 113 ms in the bar arm and 415 ms in the control arm; the gap between the arm means is 23641 ms, above the larger noise. Budget caps were 4000 MB, not the proposal's 6000, on a 16096 MB host shared with other builders; the peak RAM of any run was 1235.754 MB. Nothing was held out: the same file on the same host was both tuned and timed, so the unseen host is his PC at its next gate.
